what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 2 of 2: Does the member's pull between two slow bodies carry the velocity-dependent terms that make a pull-bound pair fall like one body?. LANDED FIRST: origin/main is the science authority; read each named note as landed (git show origin/main:docs/<note>) before any PR branch, and where a PR's wording differs from the landed text, the landed text controls. Blocks 115, 136, 138, 140, 142 and 143 are OPEN hand-off PRs (#9157, #9196, #9200, #9203, #9227, #9229): read them on their branches (gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName; git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>). Block 115 is a harvest of Grok-refereed attempts; blocks 136-143 are the supervisor's own derivations (Claude), NOT refereed by another family; nothing in them is adopted. SETTING: block 136 (PR #9196): at the closing ratio beta = -alpha with alpha = K/4, the member's constraints are kept with a bond shift N coupled to the symmetric momentum P^B = P'' + (1/4) curl S~ (block 138), the clock (lapse-like multiplier u) sourced by the energy e' and the lengths by the stress Theta; block 140: the walk's exact boost charge. The clock's weak-field law is instantaneous (an elliptic constraint), like a potential. A pair bound only by an instantaneous term has a weight W = E0 d^2E/dK^2 at rest that differs from one by about its binding fraction, W = 1 + <U>/(2m) - <T>/m at leading order for slow constituents (the static-binding expectation; see refill o's problem the-inertia-of-a-static-binding); in a theory with one light cone the pull's velocity-dependent parts (carried by the shift and the lengths) restore W = 1 at first order in the coupling. TASK: (a) at long wavelength and first order in 1/K, integrate out the member (clock u, shift N, lengths h at the closing ratio, alpha = K/4) between two slow massive bodies (energies e_i, momenta p_i, stresses p_i p_j/E) and give the two-body interaction to order v^2, exactly in the member's parameters; (b) decide whether, with it, a pull-bound pair's weight is one at first order in the binding (the first-order velocity-dependent terms of a one-light-cone theory), or state which term is missing; (c) if the shift were absent (relabellings in time not absorbed), what changes. HIT: (a) and (b) exact at the stated order, with exact checks. UPDATE (amendment s): block 144 (PR #9230, the supervisor's own derivation, not refereed by another model family) now claims (a) at alpha = K/4 the member's exchange between sources that keep the books is (1/(2K)) [T'.T - (1/2) T' T] / (p^2 - omega^2), with or without the shift, and two slow bodies feel (m1 m2 / (16 pi K r)) [1 + (3/2)(v1^2 + v2^2) - (7/2) v1.v2 - (1/2)(n.v1)(n.v2)]; (b) for any first-order pull (k/r)[1 + a(v1^2 + v2^2) + b v1.v2 + c (n.v1)(n.v2)] a bound pair's weight along P is W = 1 + [(1 + 2(2a + b))<U> + (1 + 2c)<U_P>]/M with U_P = -k (n.P)^2 / r, so pull-bound pairs have weight one along every axis at first order; (c) without the shift the pull is unchanged, and lengths drifting linearly in time by a transverse relabelling act on moving content as -xi.P. Make your own plan first; then check block 144 independently (a different gauge, a direct solution of the constraints, or a direct bound-state computation of W are welcome), or find an error in it; a confirmed or refuted block 144 is the HIT. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/the-members-velocity-dependent-pull/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes AS LANDED ON MAIN (git show origin/main:<note>); use a PR branch (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName,state) only for a note that is not on main; any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/the-members-velocity-dependent-pull/<name>/check.py"
